rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah may be parsed as appositive to “your Lord”: the shift names the one owed obedience both by lordship and by divine perfection; the relative clause signals attributes and grounds worship.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون اسم الجلالة بدلا من

words: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make Allah the subject, with the relative clause adjectival and “that is Allah, your Lord” as predicate, or make the relative clause itself the predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون اسم الجلالة مبتدأ والموصول صفة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers treating the sentence as a fresh explanatory statement over apposition, since it better exposes their ingratitude, suits the argument’s proofs, and leads into the description of God as creator.
rows.anchor: واعتبار الجملة مستأنفة أحسن من اعتبار اسم الجلالة بدلا لأنه أنسب بالتوقيف على سوء شكرهم

words: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل والنهار
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading, the punishment for arrogance follows because the offenders disbelieved God’s blessing in making night and day for them.
rows.anchor: أي تسببوا لأنفسهم بذلك العقاب لأنهم كفروا نعمة الله إذ جعل لهم الليل والنهار

words: إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage divides people into those grateful for God’s blessing and those who deny it, paralleling the preceding division into believers and deniers of God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: فقد سجلت هذه الآية على الناس

words: إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reminds creation of God’s favor, as indicated by its purpose clause and concluding statement that most people do not give thanks.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية للتذكير بنعمة الله تعالى على الخلق كما اقتضاه لام التعليل

words: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل والنهار
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are immense cosmic acts and blessings that display their maker’s power; their alternation balances light and darkness, heat and cold, making earth fit for growth and ripening fruit.
rows.anchor: فهما تكوينان عظيمان دالان على عظيم قدرة مكونهما ومنظمهما وجاعلهما متعاقبين

words: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night allows people and animals to rest and restore nervous and sensory activity; without darkness, sleep would be incomplete and recovery weak, hastening decline and shortening human life.
rows.anchor: من مصالح سكان العالم سكون الإنسان والحيوان في الليل لاسترداد النشاط العصبي

words: وجعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight lets people and animals spread out and distinguish things, enabling work, travel, settlement, and the social order; humans need light for their naturally social labor and livelihood.
rows.anchor: ومنها انتشار الناس والحيوان في النهار وتبين الذوات بالضياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage continues the creation narrative: created worlds establish God’s exclusive divinity, and the argument now shifts from created entities to their states, moving from celestial conditions to earthly ones.
rows.anchor: الآية عطف القصة على القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse returns from third-person narration to direct address, resuming the audience-facing mode used earlier when challenging them about creation.
rows.anchor: من أسلوب الغيبة من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Signs” means proofs; they are attributed to God because they demonstrate His existence and oneness.
rows.anchor: وإضافتها إلى ضمير الله لأنها دليل على وحدانيته وعلى وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variation of night and day is a sign of power that no one but God can produce, and so proves His exclusive creative act and divinity; Ibn ʿĀshūr points to the earlier discussion in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الليل والنهار آية من آيات القدرة التي لا يفعلها غير الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon signify their regular, continuing motion here, not their creation, which was already covered by the making of the heavens; the sun is one of the seven heavens and the moon follows it.
rows.anchor: ابتداء هنا حركتهما المنتظمة المستمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No particular sunrise, setting, or orbit is specified so their conditions of motion remain available as the primary evidence; mentioning their creation also reinforces the earlier statement about the heavens and completes the meaning.
rows.anchor: ولخلقهما تأكيد لما استفيد من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Humbled” and “shook” form a personifying metaphor: the earth is pictured as a person first abject, then shaking the shoulders, with each image-part mapped to the earth.
rows.anchor: مكنية بأن شبهت بشخص كان ذليلا ثم صار مهتزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It shook” points to vegetation appearing and moving on the earth; “it swelled” adds that the earth puffs up with water and rises.
rows.anchor: لأن المقصود من الاهتزاز هو ظهور النبات عليها وتحركه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the word with a hamza after the bāʾ, from the hamzated verb meaning “to rise.”
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر { وربأت } بهمزة بعد الموحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection proof is embedded within the argument for God’s exclusive creation and governance, following the Qur’an’s varied style and use of opportunities to guide toward truth.
rows.anchor: إدماج لإثبات البعث في أثناء الاستدلال على تفرده تعالى بالخلق والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection statement begins a new sentence; the analogy between two acts of revivification motivates it, and emphasis answers the audience’s denial of raising the dead.
rows.anchor: والجملة استئناف ابتدائي والمناسبة مشابهة الإحياءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative form of the subject explains the predicate: rain brings seeds inside the earth to sprout, and this is metaphorically called “reviving” the earth.
rows.anchor: وتعريف المسند إليه بالموصولية لما في الموصول من تعليل الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving earth by rain supplies a likeness-based argument for the possibility of resurrecting the dead; this analogy draws the conclusion closer but is persuasive rather than demonstrative, fitting the deniers’ appeal to customary improbability.
rows.anchor: ثم ارتقي من ذلك إلى جعل ذلك الذي سمي إحياء لأنه شبيه الإحياء دليلا على إمكان إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing affirmation that God has power over everything makes this otherwise persuasive analogy forceful: the creator alone can perform both the lesser and greater act, so neither exceeds His power.
rows.anchor: فالمشبه به حيث كان لا يقدر على فعله إلا الخالق الذي اتصف بالقدرة التامة لذاته

none: This segment contains only Qurʾānic text and page markers, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God knows everything is an explanatory resumption grounding the allocation of provision “to whom He wills”: distribution follows His knowledge of what suits each person, as 42:27 explains.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني هو كالعلة لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from bodily blessings to the spiritual blessing of Islam, addressing the Messenger and believers to honor the religion while indirectly censuring the unbelievers who reject it.
rows.anchor: انتقال من الامتنان بالنعم الجثمانية إلى الامتنان بالنعمة الروحية بطريق الإقبال على خطاب الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He legislated” means He clarified the paths of what He charged them with; the root denotes making a broad path, then came to mean establishing laws and religions, a metaphor for clarification.
rows.anchor: أوضح وبين لكم مسالك ما كلفكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The religion” is a generic definite noun covering the earlier divinely revealed religions, while “from” is partitive.
rows.anchor: وهو يعم الأديان الإلهاية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recommendation is a command coupled with exhortation; Islam is a religion like the one Noah was commanded and urged to follow, expressed either with an omitted “like” or an implicit simile treated as identity.
rows.anchor: الأمر بشيء مع تحريض على إيقاعه والعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction can be understood as “the same as what Noah was charged with”; this kind of compressed comparison is common, illustrated by Waraqa ibn Nawfal’s phrase about the revelation sent to Jesus.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الناموس الذي أنزل على عيسى

words: وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religions match in core divine attributes, monotheism, the five necessities, and further needs required for human order; each earlier religion’s equivalent is present in Islam.
rows.anchor: المماثلة في أصول الدين مما يجب لله تعالى من الصفات

words: وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier religions taught monotheism, belief in resurrection and the afterlife, general piety, obedience, avoidance of prohibitions, and customary virtues; their details and branches differed, as the earlier scriptures confirm.
rows.anchor: فالأديان السابقة كانت تأمر بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam preserves the shared fundamentals while differing from earlier religions in the scope of particular branches; this law also distinguishes itself through reasoned rulings, blocking harmful means, evidence-based inquiry, removing hardship, leniency, and close fit with human nature.
rows.anchor: ودين الإسلام لم يخل عن تلك الأصول وإن خالفها في التفاريع

words: أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if “that” is explanatory, the resemblance concerns the following command: every messenger was charged to establish the revealed religion and avoid division; either way, Islam continues the earlier religions’ good in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: أو المراد المماثلة فيما وقع عقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is named because he was the first messenger sent to humanity, so his religion is the foundation of the religions; the author links this sequence with 4:163.
rows.anchor: لأن نوحا أول رسول أرسله الله إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s religion is the root of ḥanīfism, spread among Arabs through Ishmael, and remained familiar through pilgrimage, circumcision, hospitality, and chivalry.
rows.anchor: ولأن دين إبراهيم هو أصل الحنيفية وانتشر بين العرب بدعوة إسماعيل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is included because his religion had the broadest body of legal rulings among earlier religions.
rows.anchor: ودين موسى هو أوسع الأديان السابقة في تشريع الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is included because his religion immediately preceded Islam, with no other religion between them, and because the sequence prepares Jews and Christians to be invited to Islam.
rows.anchor: وأما دين عيسى فلأنه الدين الذي سبق دين الإسلام ولم يكن بينهما دين آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing Muhammad’s revelation after Noah’s pairs the first and final religions to signal Islam’s finality, then places the three intervening religions between them as a deliberate arrangement.
rows.anchor: وتعقيب ذكر دين نوح بما أوحي إلى محمد عليهما السلام للإشارة إلى أن دين الإسلام هو الخاتم للأديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without this ordering rationale, Islam would have been mentioned first, as it is in 4:163 and 33:7.
rows.anchor: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيئين من بعده

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that Muhammad is placed first in the covenant list in 33:7 to show his superiority, since that passage enumerates those bound by the covenant.
rows.anchor: الكشاف } في آية الأحزاب أن تقديم ذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the order instead presents Islam as the original, upright religion sent first through Noah and finally through Muhammad, with the other named religions between them.
rows.anchor: وأما آية سورة الشورى فإنما أوردت في مقام وصف دين الإسلام بالأصالة والاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What We revealed to you” is the Qur’an already revealed before this verse, including its rulings; it is coordinated with Noah’s charge because it adds detailed elaboration.
rows.anchor: هو ما سبق نزوله قبل هذه الآية من القرآن بما فيه من أحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding three consecutive instances of the same relative form could explain the variation, but the author favors a subtle semantic distinction between the forms.
rows.anchor: وقد يظهر في بادىء الرأي أنه مجرد تفنن بتجنب تكرير الكلمة ثلاث مرات متواليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ladhī is the definite relative form identifying something known through its clause; mā began as a general, ambiguous noun needing a description, then often functioned as a relative.
rows.anchor: وأخواته هي الأصل في الموصولات فهي موضوعة من أصل الوضع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and others parse the mā in “God’s excellent counsel” as an indefinite “thing,” described by the following clause.
rows.anchor: عند الزمخشري وجماعة إذ قدروه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh reads mā in “this is what is ready with me” as “a thing”; the following anonymous poetic line likewise uses mā for something beneficial, with “beneficial” qualifying it.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه في قوله تعالى : هذا ما لدي عتيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā suits the old laws, no longer known except in general terms, while al-ladhī suits Muhammad’s familiar, current law; the author suggests this may be an overlooked subtlety of Qur’anic inimitability.
rows.anchor: لمناسبة أنها شرائع بعد العهد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural in “what We revealed to you” is iltifāt.
rows.anchor: وفي العدول من الغيبة إلى التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted anonymous poem uses mā for “a thing” and the adjective “beneficial” to describe it, illustrating the original indefinite sense of the relative form.
rows.anchor: لما نافعع يسعى اللبيب فلا تكن لشيء بعيد نفعه الدهر ساعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four earlier laws are described with “charged” while Muhammad’s is “revealed” because the former were temporary, awaiting a later law, like a trust held until its owner arrives; the wording also echoes 42:3.
rows.anchor: وفي جانب شريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل الإيحاء

words: أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That you establish the religion” may be a verbal noun clause functioning as an appositive to the first or final mā; coordination makes it apply equally to all the charges under “He legislated.”
rows.anchor: مصدرية ، فإنها قد تدخل على الجملة

words: أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “that” may explain “charged,” which implies speech: God charged every named messenger to establish the religion and unite around it.
rows.anchor: لأنه يتضمن معنى القول دون حروفه

words: أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the explanatory reading, earlier religions shared the obligation to maintain their revealed religion, while the broad command is specified by each religion’s own branches.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه يقتضي أن ما حكي شرعه في الأديان السابقة هو هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing something means making it stand; here it is a metaphor for taking care to practice it, as in the phrase “they establish prayer.”
rows.anchor: وهي استعارة للحرص على العمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative “establish” addresses the communities of the named messengers, though their communities were not mentioned explicitly; the command to convey implies them.
rows.anchor: أمم أولئك الرسل ولم يسبق لهم ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against division follows the command to establish the religion.
rows.anchor: وأعقب الأمر بإقامة الدين بالنهي عن التفرق في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Division is the opposite of gathering; originally it means bodies moving apart, and by metaphor it describes strong differences in circumstances and opinions.
rows.anchor: تباعد الذوات ، أي اتساع المسافة بينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers communities splitting over belief in or rejection of their messengers, and believers forming sects over religion’s principles, rules, or aims, which can disable and undermine its foundations.
rows.anchor: ويشمل التفرق بين الذين آمنوا بأن يكونوا نحلا وأحزابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition means not to divide over carrying out the religion, with some working to establish it while others hold back; agreement channels and strengthens effort, as each member helps the rest.
rows.anchor: ولا تتفرقوا في إقامته بأن ينشط بعضهم لإقامته ويتخاذل البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Division wastes religious affairs and breeds enmity that can lead people to plot against one another; the Qur’an similarly warns that disputation brings failure and loss of strength.
rows.anchor: أما إذا حصل التفرق والاختلاف فذلك مفضض إلى ضياع أمور الدين في خلال ذلك الاختلاف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when God wants good for someone, He grants that person understanding of religion; differences in legal branches based on scholars’ reasoning count as such religious learning.
rows.anchor: وأما الاختلاف في فروعه بحسب استنباط أهل العلم بالدين فذلك من التفقه الوارد فيه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about Islam being difficult for the polytheists interrupts the connection between legislating religion and the following account of their division; it also answers why they rejected a religion supported by prior revelations.
rows.anchor: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It was hard” means difficult, like “heavy”: they could not accept the call. It metaphorically describes what the soul finds unwelcoming, and “upon” reflects the included sense of weight.
rows.anchor: عجزوا عن قبول ما تدعوهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite relative “what” presents the Islamic call as something the polytheists denied, found strange, and considered impossible.
rows.anchor: اعتبارا بنكران المشركين لهذه الدعوة واستغرابهم إياها

words: كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reason the call seemed difficult was its messenger: they objected that he was a human like them and not one of the leading men from the two towns.
rows.anchor: جهة الداعي لأنه بشر مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection concerned revelation’s form: the polytheists expected a book sent down all at once and demanded one, angels, sight of God, or direct speech from Him.
rows.anchor: وجهة ما به الدعوة فإنهم حسبوا أن الله لا يخاطب الرسل إلا بكتاب ينزله إليه دفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third objection was the message’s substance, which opposed their desires: they protested against one God and mocked the prospect of being created anew after death.
rows.anchor: ومن جهة ما تضمنته الدعوة مما لم تساعد أهواؤهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense verb indicates that the Prophet’s invitation was renewed and continued over time.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على تجدد الدعوة واستمرارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanatory resumption answers why Islam’s call seemed difficult: God selects whom He wills, so the polytheists were not selected or destined for guidance because they remained distant from it.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني جواب عن سؤال من يسأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement rebuts a claim underlying their denial of the Messenger: God chooses whom He wills and need not follow their conventions about social rank or leadership.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ردا على إحدى شبههم الباعثة على إنكارهم رسالته بأن الله يجتبي من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ means drawing near and choosing; God chooses those He guides to His religion from among those who turn to Him, and knows the inward secrets of creation.
rows.anchor: ومن يشاء الله اجتباءه من هداه إلى دينه ممن ينيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the divine subject before the verbal predicate implies exclusivity, answering those who denied that God would send a human and judged the weak believers inferior to themselves.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه وهو اسم الجلالة على الخبر الفعلي لإفادة القصر ردا على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse connects back to the prohibition on division, with intervening material parenthetical; an omitted “then they divided” is understood before “they divided.”
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who divided are the same communities addressed in the command to establish religion: God instructed the earlier peoples through their messengers.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى ما عاد إليه ضمير
